QF.id: AIFM CII Legal Documents and Negotiations_1

question.text: Mr. Arvind Menon is setting up 'Lotus Bharat Growth AIF' as a Category II AIF under a trust structure. Which document is executed between the settlor and the trustee to bring the AIF into legal existence, and what is the key follow-up action mandated by the SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: A Trust Indenture (Trust Deed); the trust deed is required to be registered as per the AIF Regulations.
A Limited Liability Partnership Deed; registration with the Registrar of Companies (ROC).
A Memorandum and Articles of Association; filing with SEBI within 15 days of execution.
An Investment Management Agreement; lodgement with the depository participant.

explanation.text: The Logic: For a trust-form AIF, the constitutional document is the Trust Indenture executed between the settlor (who settles the initial sum) and the trustee. Under the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the trust deed must be registered. It is also the instrument of trusteeship and must conform to the 'determinate' status of its corpus for Income Tax Act, 1961 purposes. The Trap: LLP Deed + ROC applies to LLP-form AIFs; MoA-AoA applies to company-form AIFs — both are constitutional but not for a trust. The IMA is a separate contract between trustee and manager and is NOT the constitutional document. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C (All-Cat AIF Manager) tests all three constitutional forms; XIX-D (Cat I/II only) emphasises the trust form because most Indian Cat I/II AIFs are trusts. XIX-A Distributor exam asks the same vocabulary at a lighter depth. Manager's Pro-Tip: As a Cat I/II manager, push for trust-form from day one: it ring-fences your fiduciary/breach liability from the AIF's because you are a counterparty service provider, not a director/designated partner. That is precisely why the majority of Indian AIFs are trusts.
